title: PHP Core
intro: Applies to: every PHP class, production code and tests, whatever the framework. These rules hold in Laravel and Symfony alike; framework overlays name the framework-specific calls (`orchestration-di.md` for Laravel, the `symfony-kanon` skill's `references/symfony.md` for Symfony).

Lane boundaries: this family owns the plain-PHP file shape (`strict_types`, `final readonly`, constructor promotion) for every framework, in its File shape section; `orchestration-di.md` owns the Laravel calls (`app()`, `resolve()`, facades, helpers) and the Laravel-only file kinds (migrations, factories, config).

entries.rule: Production classes **MUST NOT** locate services at runtime; dependencies come through the constructor. A located dependency is hidden from the constructor signature, so readers and tests cannot see what the class needs. Overlays: Laravel `app()` / `resolve()` (`orchestration-di.md`), Symfony `$container->get()` (`symfony-kanon`).
entries.why: A located dependency is hidden from the constructor signature, so readers and tests cannot see what the class needs

checks.coverage: Flags calls to app(), resolve() and $container->get() in production classes.

entries.lane_note: The Laravel calls (`app()`, `resolve()`, facades, helpers) are owned by `orchestration-di.md`; the plain-PHP file shape is in this family's File shape section. Laravel overlay: ORCH-008 (its `app()`, `resolve()`, `collect()` item).

entries.rule: Classes **MUST NOT** implement static `getInstance()` singletons; shared instances **MUST** be registered in the container. A container singleton binding (`$this->app->singleton(...)` in a service provider, as `integrations.md` does for connectors) is the sanctioned form, not the banned pattern.

checks.coverage: Flags a static getInstance() method on any class.

entries.rule: A class **SHOULD NOT** extend another class only to reuse one of its methods; inject the collaborator instead.
An optional collaborator **MAY** be replaced with a Null Object implementing the same interface instead of null checks in every method.
Preconditions **SHOULD** be handled with early-return guard clauses instead of nested ifs.
Code **SHOULD NOT** chain through several objects to reach a value (`a->b()->c()->d()`); ask the nearest object for what you need.
A readonly class **SHOULD** hold immutable collections or copies, not mutable objects that callers can change. `readonly` only freezes the property, not the object behind it.
entries.why: `readonly` only freezes the property, not the object behind it

entries.rule: A method **SHOULD NOT** both change state and return data for display. A command **MAY** return the id it created or the outcome or decision of the change (see the handler Result DTO rule in `orchestration-di.md` and the command/query slices in `architecture.md`).
A module **MUST** be named after the business capability in the domain's own language, not after a technical role.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-002. Symfony counterpart: SYM-100 (one root namespace per capability, listed in `modules.php`); the `modules.php` listing stays in SYM-100.

entries.rule: A project **SHOULD** keep a domain glossary (ubiquitous language table) in its docs; a change that introduces a new context **SHOULD** add its key terms there.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-004. The Laravel entry says "a slice that introduces a new context"; the php-core wording says "a change" because a slice is a Laravel vertical-slice term.

entries.rule: Classes, methods, commands and events **MUST** be named after the business language of their context.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-013. ARCH-013 also lists `routes` and `abilities` ("Classes, methods, commands, events, routes, and abilities"); those two are Laravel-only and stay there, and route naming stays owned by `http-api.md`.

entries.rule: Technical, ETL or CRUD jargon **MUST NOT** be used in a name where a domain term exists: `Manager`, `Processor`, `Helper`, `Util`, `Registry`, `Resolver`, `Transformer`, `Ingest`, `Upsert`, `Outcome`, generic `Service`. A name fixed by a framework or library contract is exempt.

checks.coverage: Fails on a class name ending in one of the listed terms. Does not cover method or parameter names, whether a domain term exists, or names a framework contract fixes (allow-list those).

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-014. The exemption covers framework types such as an `ArgumentResolver` or a service locator, which have no domain term. The list keeps `Outcome` as in ARCH-014; it bans the word in a name, while PHP-008 and MD-031 use "outcome" only in prose, so they do not clash.

entries.rule: Methods and parameters **MUST** be named after the value actually passed, not aspirational domain language the value is not (`forGuest(int $guestId)`, not `forVip(int $guestId)` when the argument is a plain guest id).
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ARCH-015.

entries.rule: `declare(strict_types=1);` **MUST** open every PHP file.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: report a PHP file whose first statement is not declare(strict_types=1).

examples.bad:
<?php

namespace Booking;

final class Reservation {}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Booking;

final class Reservation {}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-011. ORCH-011's second sentence ("This family owns the file-shape rules for the whole codebase (models, migrations, factories, config, tests included)") is Laravel framing and stays in the Laravel entry; php-core now owns the plain-PHP file shape for every framework.

entries.rule: Comments **MUST NOT** narrate what the next line does and **MUST NOT** form step-by-step blocks. A brief why-comment (workaround, ordering constraint), a short class-level PHPDoc, or a type-only PHPDoc such as an array shape (PHP-018) **MAY** exist.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-017. The type-only PHPDoc carve-out keeps this rule consistent with PHP-018.

entries.rule: A project **MUST NOT** define traits of its own; traits from the framework or a package **MAY** be used. Shared behavior goes into a class that is injected, not a trait.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: report a trait declared in application code.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-012. Its allowed-trait list (`HasFactory`, `SoftDeletes`, `RefreshDatabase`) is Laravel-only and stays there; php-core allows framework and package traits without naming any. This rule newly binds Symfony: SYM-110 only says the Foundry `ResetDatabase` and `Factories` traits are deprecated.

entries.rule: A DTO **MUST** be a `final readonly class` with constructor property promotion and explicit types.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-024 (no subject in that entry; ORCH-012 also covers it). Symfony counterpart: SYM-015, SYM-068. Scoped to DTOs: the carve-outs in ORCH-012 (queued jobs and queued listeners that may drop `readonly`) and SYM-015 (entities, console commands extending a non-readonly base) are not DTOs and stay there. MD-024 also lists value objects; those are left to the value-object rules.

entries.rule: Complex array parameters and returns **MUST** carry array-shape PHPDoc (`@param list<Guest>`, `@return array<string, int>`).

checks.coverage: Report array parameters and return types that have no PHPDoc value type.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-033.

entries.rule: Condition-plus-action **MUST** live on the domain object (Tell, Don't Ask): `$reservation->confirm($now)`, never `if ($reservation->isPending()) { $reservation->markConfirmed(); }` in the caller; entities **MUST NOT** be anemic data holders, and logic spanning several aggregates **MUST** live in a handler.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-005 and the condition-plus-action half of MD-006. Symfony counterpart: SYM-064. Finders are left out of this entry on purpose: MD-006 puts finders on the model while SYM-064 says "finders MUST NOT live on the entity", so each overlay keeps its own finder rule. Logic spanning several aggregates stays in a handler, as in MD-006 and SYM-064. PHP-006 (do not chain through objects) is a different rule.

entries.rule: Comparisons **SHOULD** hide behind intention-revealing methods on the owning object (`$stay->overlaps($other)`, `$a->isHigherThan($b)`), not raw attribute comparisons in the caller. A primitive validity guard on a single scalar **MAY** stay inline.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-007, which says "in an orchestrator"; this entry says "in the caller" so it holds outside the orchestrator pattern. Symfony counterpart: none.

entries.rule: Domain objects **SHOULD** be created through a named constructor that returns a valid object, not `new` plus setters, with a private constructor wherever no framework or ORM needs to instantiate the class itself.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-027 (and MD-016 for read models). Carve-out that stays in the framework entries: Eloquent models keep a public constructor because the framework instantiates them, so this entry does not require a private constructor where the framework or ORM instantiates the class. Doctrine entities may use a private constructor. Symfony counterpart: none. Value objects are covered by PHP-026 and PHP-027; their public constructors are not a breach.

entries.rule: Enums **MUST** be backed, case names **MUST** be UPPER_CASE (`case CONFIRMED = 'confirmed'`), and the class name carries no `Enum` suffix.

checks.coverage: Custom rule: report a non-backed enum, a case name that is not UPPER_CASE, or an enum class name ending in `Enum`.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-017. Symfony counterpart: none. No Symfony entry states a case-naming rule, but the Symfony examples in SYM-008, SYM-044, SYM-061 and SYM-064 use PascalCase cases (`PostAbility::Publish`, `SubscriptionStatus::Cancelled`); that is a decision for the owner.

entries.rule: A user-facing enum **MUST** provide a `label()` (or equivalent) method, so display text lives with the cases and not in a `match` at each call site.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-018. Symfony counterpart: none. FIL-013 (the Filament label interface) is Filament-only and stays there.

entries.rule: A stateful field that could grow past two states **MUST** be a status enum, not a boolean flag: `status` (`PENDING`/`CONFIRMED`/`CANCELLED`), never a new `$isActive`-style flag.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-019. Symfony counterpart: SYM-082 (its mapping half: a string column mapped to a backed enum with an index). This entry is the modeling half only. MD-019's per-state `isActive()`-style helpers on the model and its `is_active` column ban stay in MD-019, and the column mapping stays in SYM-082.

entries.rule: Domain constants **MUST** be referenced through their enum, or through a class constant on a dedicated class where the values are an open set (capability names), never string literals scattered through the code.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-020. Symfony counterpart: none. The class-constant allowance keeps this entry consistent with AUTH-006 ("a typed constant") and SYM-061 ("a class constant or a backed-enum ->value"), which name a constant for capability names, so a constant on a dedicated class is not banned. MD-020 itself says "through their enum" and stays stricter in Laravel.

entries.rule: Values with format rules (email, money, date ranges) **SHOULD** be value objects validated once in their constructor, not strings re-checked in each method.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-025. Symfony counterpart: none.

entries.rule: Invariants across related fields (check-in before check-out) **MUST** be enforced in a value object's constructor, not only in the request validation layer, which never runs for imports, jobs or console input.
entries.why: never runs for imports, jobs or console input
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-026 (which names Form Request, Laravel-only; this entry says "the request validation layer"), plus HTTP-014. Symfony counterpart: SYM-045. The field-level rule that stays on the request even when a value object enforces it is HTTP-014 and SYM-045, and stays in those entries.

entries.rule: A result or value object **SHOULD** own the interpretation of its own data (`wasRejected()`, `isHigherThan()`) rather than making consumers branch on raw fields.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-028. Symfony counterpart: none. MD-028's carve-out "events stay method-free" is not part of this entry; it belongs to MD-023 and SYM-023, which stay as they are.

entries.rule: An outcome the caller handles in the same flow (try the next room, show a price without discount) **SHOULD** be returned as a result object, one `final readonly` class per outcome; a broken rule that ends the use case **MUST** throw a domain exception.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-031. Partly covered by PHP-008, which lets a command return the outcome or decision of the change; this entry says when that outcome is a result object and not an exception, and does not restate PHP-008. Symfony counterpart: SYM-017 narrows Symfony command handlers to void (they return nothing, so the caller creates the id), as #62 decision 6 narrowed PHP-008 for Symfony; this entry applies where the deciding method's return value reaches the caller. No Symfony entry changes.

entries.rule: Domain code **MUST NOT** throw framework or generic exceptions (`\RuntimeException`, an HTTP exception) for business rules; it **MUST** throw a named domain exception. The not-found case of a plain id lookup is left to the framework overlay.
allowed_in: plain id lookups: the not-found case is owned by the framework overlay

checks.coverage: Custom rule: report a thrown framework or generic exception in domain classes; the not-found exception of a plain id lookup stays allowed.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: MD-032, MD-030 and ORCH-006 (a plain id lookup keeps `findOrFail()` and no bespoke not-found exception). Symfony counterpart: SYM-069, and SYM-072, which instead requires a repository method that throws a product exception for a missing row. The two overlays disagree on the plain id lookup, so this entry leaves the not-found case of a plain id lookup to the framework overlay; both MD-032/MD-030 and SYM-072 stay as they are.

entries.rule: Vendor vocabulary **MUST NOT** leak past the integration boundary: the adapter translates the vendor's statuses, codes and payload shapes into the project's own types, and domain code reaches a vendor SDK only through an adapter class the project owns.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class ConfirmStay
{
    public function __construct(private PaymentSdk $sdk) {}

    public function handle(Reservation $reservation): void
    {
        $charge = $this->sdk->charge($reservation->total());

        if ($charge['status'] === 'succeeded_pending_3ds') {
            $reservation->confirm();
        }
    }
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class ConfirmStay
{
    public function __construct(private DepositGateway $deposits) {}

    public function handle(Reservation $reservation): void
    {
        if ($this->deposits->collect($reservation->total()) === DepositResult::COLLECTED) {
            $reservation->confirm();
        }
    }
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-002. Symfony counterpart: SYM-070 and SYM-085. The Laravel connector (Saloon) wording stays in the Laravel entries.

entries.rule: An integration adapter **SHOULD** be fronted by an interface owned by its consumer when more than one module uses it or when tests need a fake.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class SendArrivalReminder
{
    public function __construct(private SmsVendorAdapter $sms) {}
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface GuestNotifier
{
    public function remind(Guest $guest, Stay $stay): void;
}

final readonly class SendArrivalReminder
{
    public function __construct(private GuestNotifier $notifier) {}
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-003. Symfony counterpart: SYM-070, which is stricter and requires an interface for every vendor SDK or HTTP client.

entries.rule: Requests and responses crossing an integration boundary **MUST** be typed objects; associative arrays **MUST NOT** cross it.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface RoomInventory
{
    public function availability(array $query): array;
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface RoomInventory
{
    public function availability(AvailabilityQuery $query): Availability;
}

final readonly class AvailabilityQuery
{
    public function __construct(
        public DateTimeImmutable $checkIn,
        public DateTimeImmutable $checkOut,
        public int $guests,
    ) {}
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-006. The Saloon `$body` property rule of INT-010 is Laravel-only and stays there.

entries.rule: Integration adapter classes **MUST** be `final readonly`, receiving their clients and contracts through the constructor.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

class SmsVendorAdapter implements GuestNotifier
{
    private ?SmsClient $client = null;
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class SmsVendorAdapter implements GuestNotifier
{
    public function __construct(private SmsClient $client) {}
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-008 (depends on the connector, which is Saloon and Laravel-only). Symfony counterpart: none; SYM-015 covers controllers, handlers, listeners, messages, events and DTOs, not gateways. File shape is owned by php-core.

entries.rule: A focused capability **SHOULD** get its own narrow interface rather than one wide interface that forces implementers and test doubles to stub methods they never use.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface GuestGateway
{
    public function notify(Guest $guest): void;
    public function verifyIdentity(Guest $guest): bool;
    public function chargeDeposit(Reservation $reservation): void;
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface GuestNotifier
{
    public function notify(Guest $guest): void;
}

interface IdentityVerifier
{
    public function verify(Guest $guest): bool;
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: INT-009. Symfony counterpart: none.

entries.rule: Domain and application code **MUST NOT** import HTTP or request-scoped types (request, response, session, kernel) or persistence-driver types (database driver, raw connection), except in adapters, controllers, read-model query classes and cross-module readers; the framework overlay names the framework imports that stay allowed.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Framework\Http\Request;
use Framework\Database\Connection;

final readonly class CancelReservation
{
    public function handle(Request $request, Connection $db): void
    {
        $db->execute('UPDATE reservations SET cancelled = 1 WHERE id = ?', [$request->input('id')]);
    }
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class CancelReservation
{
    public function __construct(private Reservations $reservations) {}

    public function handle(CancelReservationCommand $command): void
    {
        $this->reservations->get($command->reservationId)->cancel();
    }
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none (ORCH-008 is the imports half). Symfony counterpart: SYM-070. Scoped to HTTP and driver types only; framework ORM, event and contract imports are left to the overlays. Cross-module readers are the exception ISO-007 requires ("Cross-module data access MUST be read-only, via an injected `ConnectionInterface` with id-based queries").

entries.rule: Where a repository exists, it **SHOULD** expose an interface shaped by the domain and return domain types, not query builders, ORM rows or driver results.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface ReservationRepository
{
    public function query(): QueryBuilder;
    public function rows(): array;
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

interface Reservations
{
    public function get(ReservationId $id): Reservation;
    /** @return list<Reservation> */
    public function arrivingOn(DateTimeImmutable $day): array;
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none. Laravel has no repository layer (MD-006 and ORCH-006 put finders on the model, ARCH-001 bans `app/Repositories` as a dumping ground), so this rule never requires one. Symfony counterpart: SYM-083.

entries.rule: Authorization **MUST** derive from the authenticated principal, never from request input; a handler that trusts a user id, team id or role from the request body is broken.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class CancelReservation
{
    public function handle(array $input): void
    {
        $guest = $this->guests->get($input['guest_id']);
        $this->reservations->get($input['reservation_id'])->cancelBy($guest);
    }
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class CancelReservation
{
    public function handle(CancelReservationCommand $command): void
    {
        // $command->actor was taken from the authenticated principal by the controller.
        $this->reservations->get($command->reservationId)->cancelBy($command->actor);
    }
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: AUTH-001. Symfony counterpart: SYM-058.

entries.rule: Input validation (is the request well-formed) **MUST** stay at the request boundary and invariant validation (is the domain state consistent) **MUST** stay in value objects and entities, with each invariant owned by one domain class; the input layer **MAY** carry an early copy of the same check for field-level errors, but **MUST NOT** re-implement it differently.

examples.bad:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class RegisterGuest
{
    public function handle(array $input): void
    {
        if (!preg_match('/^\S+@\S+$/', $input['email'])) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('bad email');
        }
        $guest = Guest::register(new EmailAddress($input['email']));
    }
}

final readonly class EmailAddress
{
    public function __construct(public string $value)
    {
        if (!filter_var($value, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('bad email');
        }
    }
}
examples.good:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

final readonly class RegisterGuest
{
    public function handle(RegisterGuestCommand $command): void
    {
        // Shape was validated at the boundary; the value object owns what a valid email is.
        $guest = Guest::register(new EmailAddress($command->email));
    }
}

final readonly class EmailAddress
{
    public function __construct(public string $value)
    {
        if (!filter_var($value, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) {
            throw new InvalidArgumentException('Invalid email');
        }
    }
}

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none (ORCH-025 and HTTP-014 are the Laravel forms). Symfony counterpart: SYM-039 and SYM-045. The "MAY carry an early copy" clause keeps this consistent with HTTP-014 and SYM-045, which require the field rule to stay in the request class.

entries.rule: Cached payloads **MUST** stay user-agnostic: per-user data (access verdicts, ownership flags, personalization) resolves after the cache lookup, never baked into a shared cached entry.

signals: cache key without a user id
cached value holding a per-user flag

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: ORCH-035. Symfony counterpart: SYM-007. Kept in the framework entries: ORCH-035's "in the controller" placement, the Laravel `Cached{Handler}` decorator (ORCH-033) and the Symfony `query.bus` middleware (SYM-007).

entries.rule: A class whose behavior depends on the current time **MUST** receive a clock, or use the clock call its framework overlay sanctions, and **MUST NOT** construct the current time ad hoc (`new DateTimeImmutable()`, `new DateTimeImmutable('now')`, `time()`, `date()`).

checks.coverage: Flags `new DateTimeImmutable()` and `new DateTimeImmutable('now')` with no explicit time argument, and calls to `time()` and `date()` without a timestamp, in production classes. Allow-list a clock adapter.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none. Related: ORCH-008 allows a static clock call, "`now()` -> `CarbonImmutable::now()` (explicit import)"; the clause "or use the clock call its framework overlay sanctions" keeps that valid, and a static `CarbonImmutable::now()` call is not on the banned list. Symfony counterpart: SYM-003 (inject `ClockInterface`). Pure value construction from an explicit timestamp or string (`new DateTimeImmutable('2026-03-01')`) is not "the current time" and stays allowed.

entries.rule: Event listeners **MUST** stay thin: they call a handler or dispatch a command, or perform one reaction such as recording a history row or sending a message, and hold no business rules beyond deciding whether to react; a reaction that runs asynchronously **MUST** be safe to run twice (idempotent).

signals: listener with conditionals on business state
queued listener without a duplicate guard

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none. Related, not contradicted: ORCH-027 ("a dedicated `final readonly` listener records it") and ORCH-028 ("sent from a listener via an injected `Mailer`"); the one-reaction clause keeps a listener that records an audit row or sends a mail valid. Symfony counterparts: SYM-022 and SYM-025 (event bus placement and one handler per listener). MD-023 ("Decisions about an event belong in its listener.") is why the rule allows the decision to react.

entries.rule: Test method names **MUST** state the behavior with the `it_` prefix (`it_cancels_a_stay_before_check_in`), never a generic name (`test_cancel`).

checks.coverage: Flags a #[Test] method whose name does not start with it_.

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-003. Symfony counterpart: SYM-108 (PHPUnit with `#[Test]`, Pest forbidden). SYM-108 has no naming rule and its own example already uses `it_places_an_order`, so this php-core rule newly binds Symfony tests and SYM-108 does not forbid it.

entries.rule: Every behavioral change **MUST** ship with tests covering the happy path, the failure paths and the edge cases; an untested behavior is incomplete work, not a follow-up.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-007.

entries.rule: State transitions **MUST** be tested from every relevant source state, not just the happy one.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-015.

entries.rule: History and audit tests **MUST** assert the actual recorded content and metadata, not merely that a row or entry exists.
entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: TEST-016.

entries.rule: Where commands go through a bus, a test that checks a command was dispatched **SHOULD** assert it on a recording or in-memory bus (the framework's own fake counts) instead of running the handler, and a hand-written fake of a port **MUST** be kept honest by a contract test shared with the real adapter.

signals: contract test shared by fake and adapter

entries.lane_note: Laravel counterpart: none. Related, not contradicted: TEST-011 (`Event::fake()` plus `assertDispatched(...)`), TEST-012 (`Bus::assertDispatched`) and TEST-006 ("Tests MAY use facades and helpers freely"); the framework fake counts as a recording bus, so Laravel tests do not hand-build one. TEST-011 and TEST-012 are MUST and stay stricter for Laravel. Symfony counterpart: SYM-121 ("Controller tests SHOULD assert the dispatched command against an in-memory bus"). The HTTP-client fake is SYM-122 and is not named here.
